run.change_description: fix(vercel): Fix ISR path rewrite to prevent 404

summary.intent: Restore ISR-served routes on the Vercel adapter, which returned 404 after #15959 removed the unauthenticated query-parameter path override, by re-enabling that override for requests carrying `x-vercel-isr: 1`.
summary.issue_fit: Issue alignment unavailable: no originating issue; the supplied pull-request text and the commit message are the intent sources. The ISR outcome is not verifiable offline.
summary.coverage: Both changed files reviewed against the merge-base; the built handler was called in-process with stubbed virtual modules. Repository tests could not run: fixture directories are read-only in this sandbox. Uncommitted `.mcp.json` in the clone is outside the range.
check_details: Reviewer ran `node --test test/path-override-security.test.js test/isr.test.js` at the reviewed head: environmental failure, the fixture build could not create `.astro/collections` (read-only fixture directory); no test result.

Reviewer ran an in-process scratch harness against the built `dist/serverless/entrypoint.js` at the reviewed head: a request without the middleware secret but with `x-vercel-isr: 1` and `?x_astro_path=` was rewritten to the query-supplied path; the same request without the header was not.
No CI or supplied check evidence was provided; the author-reported manual Vercel deployments were not reproducible offline.

questions.title: Does Vercel strip a client-supplied x-vercel-isr header?
questions.evidence: The head now honours `x_astro_path` whenever the request has `x-vercel-isr: 1` and no valid middleware secret (`packages/integrations/vercel/src/serverless/entrypoint.ts:21-26`). Nothing in the repository sets, documents or strips that header, and the same entrypoint is the `_render` function of every build, ISR or not. An in-process call with the header and `?x_astro_path=/api/private` on `/api/public` rendered `/api/private`; without the header it rendered `/api/public`, the behaviour the #15959 test in `packages/integrations/vercel/test/path-override-security.test.js` pins.
questions.why_it_matters: If Vercel forwards a client-sent `x-vercel-isr`, any caller can again rewrite the routed path and bypass edge-middleware or firewall rules, undoing #15959, and the candidate reopens as a must-fix security finding. If Vercel strips or overwrites it, the guard is sound and only a regression test is missing.
questions.answer: A Vercel maintainer or Vercel platform documentation can state whether the edge network removes or overwrites inbound `x-vercel-isr` and sends `1` only to ISR invocations; a deployed request with a spoofed header would also settle it.

observations.fact: The change adds no test for the ISR rewrite, although `test/path-override-security.test.js` covers the sibling untrusted-override cases on `_render`.
observations.evidence: `git diff main...review-head --stat` lists only the changeset and `packages/integrations/vercel/src/serverless/entrypoint.ts`.
